channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: ₹1 crore a kilo: a Bhuj ring pitches Swiss gold
item.description: A Divya Bhaskar reporter posing as a factory owner was shown 100-gram Metalor and PAMP bars pulled from a waist belt. The seller named no bill, no certificate and payment through an angadia.

item.title: ₹20 lakh advance fee ends a ₹24 crore Surat sale
item.description: Mahidharpura police have booked two people who offered to buy a Katargam jeweller's properties for a Dubai company. The money taken was billed as a charge to unfreeze that company's account.

item.title: One lot, no estimate: Christie’s offers a Qianlong ewer
item.description: The solid-gold ewer is set with pearls, rubies, sapphires and turquoise and carries a Qianlong mark. It comes from Dr Carl Kempe's collection and sells in Hong Kong on 29 October.

item.title: HK$278m top-up lifts the Cheng vehicle to 73.57%
item.description: Chow Tai Fook Enterprises bought about 34.18 million shares at HK$8.1275 on 6 October, per the exchange's disclosure. The company is the group's construction and roads arm, not the jeweller.

item.title: Sherwood family buys back Daniel's 100 stores from PE
item.description: Palladium Equity Partners held the credit jeweller for twelve years and grew it from 73 shops. The buyer alongside the family is AJS Creations, a lab-grown e-tail group on $350 million.

item.title: £1.2 million stops short of an 8.03-carat blue's reserve
item.description: Elmwood's offered the fancy light blue in London on 1 October against an estimate of £1.5m to £2m. The highest hammer price anything in the sale did make was £13,000.

item.title: Surat's cutters ask for the 20% their wages lost
item.description: The Diamond Worker Union says factory owners cut piece pay through a four-year slowdown and have not restored it. It also expects this year's Diwali break to run 5 to 15 November.

item.title: GST Council puts 90% of export refunds on automation
item.description: India's 57th Council recommended on 8 October that provisional refunds for zero-rated supplies clear by risk-based processing without officer review. The acknowledgement clock would fall from 15 days to 10.

item.title: Nine months take 27.4% off China's brand gold counters
item.description: Brand jewellery gold peaked at 1,722 yuan a gram on 29 January and sits at the 1,250 level now. A Huaxia Times report from Shuibei puts the district's own buy-sell spread near 183 yuan on 4 October.

item.title: 81.17-carat Paraiba leads Bonhams Paris on 29 October
item.description: The neon-blue cushion-cut tourmaline carries a €60,000 to €80,000 estimate. Two unheated sapphires over 10 carats, signed Cartier and Chaumet, follow at €40,000 to €60,000 and €45,000 to €65,000.

item.title: Old gold now funds 38% of PNG Jewellers' Q2 sales
item.description: The share was 29% a year earlier, on figures still subject to auditors' limited review. Revenue rose 22.4% at PNG and more than 26% at Kalyan Jewellers in the quarter to 30 September.

item.title: Le Vian prices 17 antique-cushion styles from $1,499.99
item.description: The cut arrives at Kay Jewelers in mid-October across eight natural gemstones, from nude quartz to rose morganite. The in-store range tops out at $4,999.99, with further designs online.

item.title: Movado sells 95% of EBEL for $66.5 million, keeps 5%
item.description: The buyer group is led by F.P. Journe's parent, with Chanel and Pierre Jacques, who becomes chief executive. Movado's owned-brand sales grew 3.7% in the half year; its licensed brands grew 7.8%.

item.title: 24-carat pink diamond carries a CHF 15 million high estimate
item.description: Christie's puts the emerald-cut, fancy-intense-pink, type IIa stone in its Geneva Magnificent Jewels sale on 10 November. Bulgari set it in a ring in the 1950s for a noble family that has held it since.

item.title: 23 Blue Nile showrooms convert to stores with inventory
item.description: Signet's chief financial officer says the conversion runs over the next year or so. The digital-first division is being rebuilt around natural diamonds, and a bought-in concierge desk now staffs the bespoke requests its sales floor could not answer.

item.title: Over 190 companies and 900 stores join India's gold audit
item.description: IAGES chief executive Kaushlendra Sinha says about 150 audit firms have been trained to run the third-party checks. Thirty to forty Gujarat stores have joined, along with manufacturers in Surat, Rajkot and Ahmedabad.

item.title: HKD 1.8 million tops Poly Auction's Hong Kong jewellery sale
item.description: A Van Cleef and Arpels sapphire and diamond necklace led the 6 October High Jewelry and Important Watches sale. Burmese ruby and cabochon sapphire earrings cleared their high estimate by more than twice.

item.title: Five seized watches worth GBP 1 million go to no-reserve sale
item.description: Wilsons Auctions will sell timepieces forfeited from an HMRC payroll-fraud investigation online from 29 to 30 October. A Philippe Dufour Simplicity leads; every lot sells whatever the hammer price.

item.title: AWDC charges its EUR 40 Diamond Office fee once per shipment
item.description: The minimum fee stops applying per declaration line for polished shipments worth under EUR 100,000. It takes effect with the September invoicing cycle, on invoices issued 2 October.

item.title: Gold opens at $4,188.10 and silver gains 2.56% on Kitco
item.description: All four precious metals opened higher against the paper's prior printed marks on Friday, with platinum up the most in percentage terms. CNBC's independent feed agrees on direction on every metal.

item.title: US specialty jewelers add 5.7% in September on fewer units
item.description: Tenoris recorded close to two years of uninterrupted monthly growth, with year-to-date revenue up 8.5%. Average spend per item rose 11%; sales of lower-priced jewellery fell 11% and natural diamond jewellery slipped 0.6%.

item.title: Silver sheds 2.12% to $58.757 as gold and platinum gain
item.description: A 06:00 board stamp put gold at $4,121.00, platinum at $1,642.00 and palladium at $1,114.00. CNBC's independent quotes sat inside Kitco's own bid-ask band on all four metals.

item.title: Titan's jewellery revenue rises 21%, against 39% a year ago
item.description: Consolidated sales at India's largest jewellery retailer advanced 25% in the quarter to 30 September. Studded sales grew in the low 30s in percentage terms, and the chain added 78 stores to reach 3,758.

item.title: $50 million restarts Elizabeth Bay, Namibia's exports down 67%
item.description: Kenzoll Capital and MSF Commercials will revive the mine renamed Sperrgebiet, which holds 10.5 million carats onshore and offshore. Namibian diamond exports fell from NAD 5.1 billion in 2022 to NAD 1.7 billion in 2025.

item.title: 8.17-carat D/IF ring carries $350,000 at Christie's, no reserve
item.description: Bidding on Jewels Online opened 6 October and closes 15 October, on Christie's own calendar. The round brilliant leads more than 260 lots; the next-highest estimate in the preview tops out at $280,000.

item.title: Voutilainen 28Sport reaches $700,000, 2.9 times its estimate
item.description: Phillips' 88-lot New York Sessions sale opened 1 October and closes 9 October at 10 a.m. Eastern. Two F.P. Journe lots also sit above estimate; a Patek Philippe 5270 stays inside its $80,000 to $160,000 range.

item.title: Mejuri swaps lab-grown diamonds for sapphires in four styles
item.description: The Toronto brand put Montana stones into its Salmon Gold line, pricing two rings, a charm and earrings from $498 to $896. It invested $1.5 million in the Regeneration project in 2023.

item.title: $275.1 billion holiday forecast carries $21.3 billion in BNPL
item.description: Adobe Analytics projects a 7% rise in US online spending between 1 November and 31 December. Cyber Monday alone is forecast at $15.1 billion, the first single day above that line.

item.title: PBoC adds 740,000 ounces, the most of its 23-month run
item.description: China's gold reserve reached 77.47 million ounces at the end of September, about 2,409.59 tonnes. Foreign-exchange reserves fell $38.1 billion in the same month, and London gold closed September down 6.52%.

item.title: Perth Mint sells 47,300 ounces of gold, up 98% on August
item.description: Silver minted-product sales reached 605,408 ounces and platinum 4,711, which the Mint puts at 344% above the prior month. The first 2027 Year of the Goat coins carried the month.
